text: Thank you for bringing it up. We lost that client in March, when they changed their whole IT team. We looked into it, and we figured out that the problem was the transition. We have ruled out the same risk with our other banking clients. I can back it up with the renewal data from the last two years. Let me walk you through it, and I will follow up with the details on Friday.

When I ask a founder a hard question, I am not looking for a perfect answer. I am watching the first five seconds. The founders I trust say thank you for bringing it up, and then they tell me what they looked into and what they can back up. The ones I worry about start a long story. In my experience, a long story usually means nobody has figured it out yet.

In our due diligence, the buyer brought up a client we had lost the year before. I was ready for it. I said: we looked into it, we figured out that the problem was the transition, and we have ruled out the same risk with our other banks. Then I offered to walk them through the renewal data. It took two minutes. Later the buyer told me that answer was the moment they decided to hold off on lowering the price.
